'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[Tigray Defense Forces]] capture the [[Tigray Region|regional]] capital [[Mekelle]] after forcing [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|Ethiopian troops]] to retreat. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/06/28/world/asia/tigray-mekelle-ethiopia-retreat.html (''The New York Times'')]
**The [[Government of Ethiopia|Ethiopian government]] declares an immediate unilateral [[ceasefire]] in Tigray following the withdrawal of troops from Mekelle. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-57645282 (BBC News)]
*[[American-led intervention in the Syrian civil war]]
**The [[U.S. military]] says that it conducted [[June 2021 United States airstrike in Syria|airstrikes]] on facilities purportedly used by [[Popular Mobilization Forces|Iranian-supported militias]] near the [[Iraq–Syria border]]. [[Prime Minister of Iraq|Iraqi Prime Minister]] [[Mustafa Al-Kadhimi]] condemns the airstrikes as a "blatant and unacceptable violation of Iraqi sovereignty and Iraqi national security". [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/06/27/airstrikes-iran-syria-iraq-496651 (Politico)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/28/iraq-pm-slams-us-raids-as-flagrant-violation-of-sovereignty (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Syria]]n state media say that an air [[missile]] attack around 1 a.m. on residential houses in the countryside of [[al-Bokmal]], presumably by American warplanes, killed a child and injured three civilians. [https://sana.sy/en/?p=239498 (SANA)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]; [[2021 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks]]
**A [[suicide bomb]]er blows himself up at a busy [[intersection (road)|intersection]] in [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. No additional casualties are reported. This is the first suicide bombing in the country and comes a day after a bombing occurred at a [[Catholic Church|Catholic]] [[Church (building)|church]], seriously injuring two people. Authorities ban public gatherings for two days in response to the attacks, warning about the possibility of further incidents. The [[Islamic State's Central Africa Province]] claimed responsibility for both bombings. [https://apnews.com/article/islamic-state-group-africa-religion-3fd955e71f90217141bec90026f70a39 (AP)][https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-06-29/islamic-state-group-says-its-behind-congo-suicide-bombing (USNews)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Elephant & Castle fire]]
**A fire occurs in an [[automobile repair shop]] near [[Elephant & Castle tube station]] in [[London]], UK, causing disruption to transport. Six people are injured. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/jun/28/fire-in-elephant-and-castle-south-london (''The Guardian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 8,364 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 896,770. [https://bdnews24.com/health/2021/06/28/bangladesh-posts-record-8364-virus-cases-in-a-day-another-104-die (BDNews24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia]]
****[[President of Indonesia|President]] [[Joko Widodo]] announces that the [[National Agency of Drug and Food Control of Indonesia|Indonesian Food and Drug Authority]] approves the emergency use of the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] vaccine for children aged 12 to 17 years old. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5623197/tuh-kan-bener-bpom-sudah-izinkan-vaksin-sinovac-untuk-anak-12-17-tahun (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] surpasses 5,000 deaths from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/06/28/malaysias-covid-19-deaths-surpass-5000/1985625 (''Malay Mail'')]
** [[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] announces [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia|vaccination]] will be [[vaccination policy|mandatory]] for all workers in the [[Aged care in Australia|aged care sector]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jun/28/vaccination-mandatory-for-aged-care-workers-as-astrazeneca-made-available-to-all-australian-adults (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] locks down the Qauia settlement near [[Suva]], amid a substantial increase in the number of cases of COVID-19 in the country, which is reporting up to 300 new cases a day, with several clusters and spread of the [[Delta variant]]. The government alleges that the infections began to increase after a breach of protocol by a Navy officer. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/settlements-locked-down-fiji-endures-deadly-coronavirus-wave-2021-06-28/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] drops its [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mandatory mask wearing]] requirement in outdoor areas as all of 20 [[Regions of Italy|region]]s are classified as "white" level, signifying a low-risk region. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210628-mask-free-and-low-risk-italy-welcomewhites-milestone (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 22,868 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of daily cases since January 30. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-06-28/covid-uk-records-22868-coronavirus-cases-in-past-24-hours-highest-number-since-end-of-january (ITV News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[South Africa]] imposes an adjusted alert Level 4 for the next 14 days that includes a curfew from 9 p.m. to 4 a.m., prohibition of alcohol sales and a ban on all social gatherings in order to prevent the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]]. In addition, schools will also be closed beginning on June 30. [https://www.iol.co.za/news/alcohol-ban-schools-to-close-heres-the-level-4-restrictions-that-kick-in-on-monday-979abfd7-26c8-48ea-a44d-5be7b46013a1 (Independent Online)]
*[[2021 Western North America heat wave]]
**The temperature reaches {{convert|47.9|C|F}} in [[Lytton, British Columbia]], breaking the all-time record for hottest temperature ever recorded in Canada for the second day in a row. The temperature reached {{convert|46.6|C|F}} in Lytton on June 27, which was the previous record. [https://vancouversun.com/news/local-news/even-lytton-is-feeling-the-heat-as-records-continue-to-be-shattered (''The Vancouver Sun'')] 

'''International relations'''
*[[Ukraine–NATO relations]]
**[[Ukraine]] and [[NATO]] forces launch joint naval drills in the [[Black Sea]] codenamed ''Sea Breeze 2021''. [[Russia]] has condemned  the drills, with the [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Russian Defence Ministry]] saying that they would closely monitor the drills. [https://apnews.com/article/black-sea-ukraine-europe-government-and-politics-ea5d4e704ecce23a4d7aa7196f04ba9f (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Police in [[Hong Kong]] ban a vigil to mark the anniversary of the [[Handover of Hong Kong|British handover of the territory]] to [[China]]. In a letter addressed to the [[League of Social Democrats]], police cite "great risk to citizens" due to [[COVID-19]]. Another letter was also sent to the [[Civil Human Rights Front]] whose former and current leaders, [[Jimmy Sham]] and [[Figo Chan]], are both behind bars, the former on national security law charges and the latter convicted of unlawful assembly. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/06/28/us-hongkong-security-handover (Euronews)] [https://hongkongfp.com/2021/06/28/hong-kong-police-ban-annual-july-1-democracy-demo-citing-covid-19/ (HKFP)]
*Former [[Belarus]]ian presidential candidate [[Viktar Babaryka]] tells a court in [[Minsk]] that he is innocent of the [[corruption in Belarus|corruption]] charges against him. Babaryka was one of the main challengers to [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] and was arrested in June 2020. Babaryka says that he cannot confess to crimes that he did not commit and faces up to 15 years' imprisonment if he is found guilty. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/jailed-belarusian-presidential-contender-tells-court-he-is-innocent-2021-06-28/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Supreme Court of Mexico]] decriminalizes the [[recreational drug use|recreational use]] of [[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] for adults. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210628-mexico-top-court-decriminalizes-recreational-marijuana-use (France 24)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Samoan constitutional crisis]]
**The [[Supreme Court of Samoa]] rules that the swearing in of the [[Faʻatuatua i le Atua Samoa ua Tasi|FAST]] party-led government on May 24th was illegal. However, the court also orders that the [[Legislative Assembly of Samoa]] sit within seven days, giving the opposition FAST, led by [[Naomi Mataʻafa]], the ability to form a new government. FAST currently holds 26 seats in parliament, while the caretaker [[HRPP]] government of [[Tuila'epa Sa'ilele Malielegaoi]] has 24 seats. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/445660/samoa-s-parliament-ordered-to-sit-within-a-week (RNZI)]
*[[2021 Swedish government crisis]]
**[[Prime Minister of Sweden|Prime Minister]] [[Stefan Löfven]] resigns after he lost a no-confidence vote on June 21. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/06/28/europe/sweden-stefan-lofven-resignation-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''Science and technology'''
*The [[Baihetan Dam]], the third largest dam in [[China]] and the [[List of largest dams|fourth largest in the world]], officially opens. [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/chinas-giant-baihetan-hydro-plant-begins-generating-power-cctv-2021-06-28/ (Reuters)]
